subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw reset or scope polling offsets when normalized `apiRoot` changes, and should `400: Logged out` during migration be treated as a nonfatal startup state?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing persisted polling watermark semantics and startup failure handling is compatibility-sensitive and needs maintainer-owned policy plus live Telegram proof.

options.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, narrowly tolerate the migration-only logged-out cleanup response, and require live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor/docs reset only
options.body: Keep runtime offsets account/token-scoped and make doctor or documentation the supported endpoint-switch reset path.

options.title: Keep current advanced behavior
options.body: Leave local Bot API endpoint migration as an operator-managed workflow and document manual cleanup expectations without runtime changes.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, narrowly tolerate the migration-only logged-out cleanup response, and require live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to Telegram polling offset scoping and recent polling/spool reliability history.
